title: Replenishment orders the right items in the right quantities
requirement: Plan: read stock levels, create requests for items at their reorder point (quantity from the planning data, whole packs, supplier minimum)

title: Approval routing follows the rule table and the organisation
requirement: Rule 8, the plan and D36: a rule is chosen by value band, spend type, category, department, location and the date it is in force, rows starting '+' add approvers; its chain becomes real people

title: Sourcing picks the right contract price, or sends the line to quotation
requirement: Plan: contract vs RFQ per line; only an active contract in force, for an active supplier, in the right unit, with the quantity break

title: GST and order arithmetic is exact, to the paisa
requirement: Rule 1: money is Decimal to paise; GST splits into CGST+SGST within the state and IGST across states; composition and unregistered suppliers charge none

title: Quote comparison recommends the right supplier and the award rules hold
requirement: Plan: collect quotes, compare, select; the recommendation is the lowest qualifying offer; an override or too few qualifying quotes needs a reason

title: The whole flow, stock level to approved purchase order, keeps its promises
requirement: Plan: nothing is lost, money reconciles, every change is audited, only eligible suppliers are asked, stock on the way is counted once

title: Repeating or racing any stage makes no duplicates
requirement: Plan: no duplicate requests, RFQs, emails or orders; document numbers have no gaps and no repeats

title: Decisions stay reproducible when the rules change
requirement: Rule 8: rules and rates are versioned data; a decision stays reproducible against the version it used

title: Every write action is open to exactly the roles the plan names
requirement: Rule 7 and the plan: requester, buyer, approver and administrator duties are separate; nobody else can do them; nobody can without logging in

title: One company cannot see another company's data
requirement: Rule 6: one database per tenant; a request without tenant context is refused; tenant A cannot read tenant B

title: Hostile text is shown as text and never run
requirement: Security: names from imported data and typed identifiers cannot inject script into the screens or SQL into the database

title: ERP demand files load exactly once, with every bad row explained
requirement: Plan P1-29: production orders with their component lines, MRP results, sales orders and the demand plan are imported from the client's ERP files; every rejected row is listed with its reason; the same ERP order is never loaded twice; a changed order is applied and listed with what changed (Q21, 20 Nov: the change propagates); one company never sees another's imports. For an IT services company the joiner kits and the joiner plan load the same way: each joiner row becomes its kit's items times the joiners, by the start date, for the joiner's department, and one material request per plan and department

title: The buying route: contract, single source, emergency, safe reorder, else quotation with the right quotes
requirement: Plan D37 / P1-33: first yes wins; Rs 25,000 agreement and reorder limit; 90 days; 80% on time; 2% price; 2 quotes from Rs 25,000 to Rs 2,00,000 and 3 above; value counted per item over 30 days; categories only stricter

title: Stock is set aside earliest need-by first and only the shortfall is bought
requirement: Plan P1-30 and step 2 of the flow: each imported production order gets a material request; the store check sets free stock aside earliest need-by first and never more than is on the shelf; only the shortfall becomes a purchase request, priced at the contract price else the last price paid else the standard price, sent to the approver the rule table names; the plan's MO-1 example (Rs 72,930 for four items short) holds; issue at production start takes exactly what was set aside; nothing is set aside or bought twice; only the store may do it

title: Shortfalls of several orders combine into one line, and the budget is checked per location
requirement: Plan P1-31 and step 3 of the flow: shortfall lines for the same item and delivery location needed within the combining window (setting, default 7 days) become one requisition line that keeps each order's own quantity; lines further apart stay separate; cancelling one order takes its part off the combined line (and the stock it held covers, earliest need-by first, the parts of the others, which are cut by as much); the budget is checked per department and per location (decision D36: warn at 90% used, over above 100%), naming the location, the department and the months of the financial year it counted; every combination and reduction is audited

title: Supplier selection: must-haves, total cost, tie-break, split only when it saves, reasons, orders per supplier
requirement: Plan step 6 / P1-34: drop quotes failing a must-have; compare total cost (GST not counted with input credit); ties by earlier delivery; split only when the saving beats the extra freight; a reason for other than the cheapest qualifying quote or too few quotes; one PO per supplier; printable RFQ per supplier

title: PO tiers by value, delivery location, touchless orders only within every limit
requirement: Plan step 7 / P1-35, D35, D36, v1.1: up to Rs 1,00,000 only a touchless order is approved, by the rule, else the purchase manager, who approves to Rs 5,00,000; director above; never the buyer who made the order; touchless for contract and safe-reorder lines within the limit, active supplier, contract room, price within 2%, budget and the autonomy gate, recorded with the facts and the rule version; delivery place on the PO
notes: The plan's four orders total Rs 85,113.40; at the dataset's rates they total Rs 84937.90. The cartons (PK-01) are at 5% GST in the dataset (the rate changed on 22 Sep 2025); the plan worked them at 18%.

title: Approval by email: the right person, a full email, one reminder, escalation on time, a code above the limit
requirement: Plan step 4 and D36: who approves follows the rule table by value, category, department and location (rows that add an approver too); each step keeps its rule row; the email carries the lines, the estimated total, the budget, why it came to this person and approve / reject / return links that work once; one reminder after a working day and escalation after two, counted on the business calendar with holidays; a one-time code above Rs 5,00,000 that is hashed, expires in 10 minutes, allows 5 tries and works once; a deputy; the requester never approves

title: Supplier confirmation: the link works once, every change is the buyer's, a new version tells the requester
requirement: Plan step 8, P1-36: accept, decline or ask for a change from a signed link that works once (or by email); each change goes to the buyer old value to new; an accepted date, quantity or price makes a new version and tells the requester; a price above tolerance needs the purchase manager; a decline goes back to the buyer to source again; dispatch notes for the store; reminders before the promised date and after it while nothing has arrived, on the business calendar, each once. Done when a date change makes PO version 2 and tells the requester

title: Service entry, the two-way match of services, receipts without an order and serial numbers are right
requirement: Plan step 9, P1-37: the requester confirms a service (quantity, percent or amount), a service invoice is matched against the order and the confirmation, an unconfirmed service cannot be invoiced, a receipt without an order needs the purchase manager's approval and an after-the-fact order, serialised items need a unique serial per unit

title: The exceptions screen lists every stuck case with the right reason, owner and age, by role
requirement: Plan step 11/12, P1-38: one list of everything stuck that needs a person (blocked invoices, goods without an order, services not confirmed, approvals past their reminder, proposals, suppliers to chase) with what, reason, owner, next step, age in working days and amount, oldest first, filtered by kind and mine, by permission

title: Received not invoiced, supplier statements, small-supplier deadlines and the order trace reconcile
requirement: Plan step 13, P1-39: received not invoiced (and the reverse) exact to the paisa with its age; a supplier's statement matched line by line with the reason for each difference; MSME invoices listed against the MSMED Act deadline (Q16); the whole chain of a document traced end to end

title: The IT services company (Brightwave) through all 13 steps in a browser: services, a serialised laptop, two-way match
requirement: Phase 1 done-when: both demo companies run through all 13 steps in the browser; services are confirmed by the requester and matched two ways; a serialised item is received with its serial; each step by its own person

title: Cancelling a production order releases its stock to the next order at once, never stocked and bought twice
requirement: Plan P1-30 and step 2 of the flow: cancelling an order releases its reservation (a reason is needed; only the store; once); the freed stock is set aside at once for the open orders earliest need-by first, each up to what it still lacks, never more than is on the shelf; a purchase request still open for that shortfall is cut by as much (set aside plus requested never exceeds the need) and the next check buys nothing; purchase requests made only for the cancelled order and not yet with the buyer are cut and cancelled (Q21, 20 Nov); issue never moves more than is set aside; the cancel is audited

title: Shortfall requests are estimated at the contract price, else the last price paid, else the standard price
requirement: Plan step 3 (estimated price): the contract price if one is valid, else the last price paid (the latest order that is not a draft and not cancelled), else the item's standard price; the estimate sets the request's value and so its approver

title: Supplier selection by weighted score, and the answer key's cheapest supplier, match an independent oracle
requirement: Plan step 6 / P1-34: quotes failing a must-have are dropped; the rest are compared on total cost or, when the company's versioned rule says so, on a weighted score of price, delivery, quality and payment terms; ties by earlier delivery; the rule version is recorded with each selection; the dataset's RFQs select the supplier its answer key names

title: Contract price versions: a draft is never used, a second person activates it, the old one ends the day before
requirement: D48: a contract price is a version; a draft is used for nothing until someone other than who stored the contract, entered a price of the version or sent it activates it; the version it replaces ends the day before it starts; prices of one supplier for an item never apply on the same day; an order keeps the version it was bought at

title: Control changes wait for a second administrator; nobody approves their own change or their own access
requirement: D-22 (second administrator): a change to rules, rule versions, policies, tolerances, automation, roles, limits, logins and managers applies only when a different administrator approves it; the proposer never approves; a rejection keeps the old value; stopping automation is immediate; an unapproved change expires after seven days; one change at a time per setting; the history shows maker and approver; nobody widens or approves their own access

title: Bank accounts: verified by a second person against a proof before anything is paid into them
requirement: DF-03 / F1: a new or changed supplier bank account is unverified; it is never planned into a payment run, advanced or written to a bank file until a person other than the one who entered or asked for it verifies it (Finance, an allowed method from `bank_verification_methods`, a proof file); a bank change after a run is approved takes that supplier out, recomputes the total and voids a file already made; lists show the last four digits; the audit never holds the whole number; another company sees nothing

title: PO makers never approve: not the order, its price, a supplier's price rise, nor as a deputy
requirement: C1 (v1.1): the people who made a purchase order (its buyer, submitter, reviser, the awarder of its quotation, who changed its buying route) never approve it, accept its price or a supplier's price rise (even within tolerance), nor stand in as a deputy; the chain skips them and goes up a tier; in the band with no approver only a touchless order is approved by the rule, any other goes to a person; accepting a price is not making the order; a refused person changes nothing
